Wattimena Sinks Littler In Wolverhampton

PDCPDC Grand Slam of DartsPDC Majors
18 November 2026
Share
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
WhatsApp
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 3:11
    Instaread

    Jermaine Wattimena sensationally ended the double-title defence of Luke Littler at the Grand Slam, with the Dutchman taking a superb and deserved 10-8 win against ‘The Nuke’ in their last 16 meeting.

    Wattimena pinned double one for a 3-2 lead at the first intermission, and a 64 checkout made it a two-leg buffer for the Dutchman, before he went seven darts into a perfect leg and settled for a 12-darter for 5-2.

    It was becoming a precession, with Wattimena making it six straight legs as he made it 7-2, but he then missed crucial darts at double, allowing Littler to break and trim his huge lead.

    Littler chipped away at that lead, closing to 9-7 with a ten-darter, and that became 9-8 with Wattimena wobbling, but he admirably held firm, and a 77 finish confirmed a famous win, and an emotional Wattimena took in the adulation of the crowd.

    Kevin Doets will be next up for Wattimena, as ‘Hawkeye’ took an assured 10-5 win against Cameron Menzies.

    Doets missed double 12 for a nine-darter early on, and took the first break of throw of the contest for a 6-4 lead.

    That became 9-4 as Doets took control, and he quickly wrapped up victory, pinning double four to end with an average north of 101.

    Gerwyn Price is on the hunt for a fourth Wolverhampton crown, and he kept Ryan Searle at arms’ length for a 10-7 win.

    Finishes of 148 and 147 helped Price to 4-1 and 5-3 leads, and a crucial 91 finish ensured he went into the interval 6-4 ahead.

    That advantage could have been widened by the Welshman, but Searle kept in touch, closing to 7-6 behind, only for an 87 finish from Price to knock the stuffing out of Searle for 9-6.

    Searle produced one last riposte, but Price wasn’t for catching, ending with a 103.31 average to power into the last eight.

    Niko Springer was first into the quarters, as the German produced a mid-match burst to take a 10-8 win against Rob Cross.

    A 116 checkout from Cross saw all of the first five legs go with throw, and after Springer took out 90, he hit the front with the first break of throw of the contest.

    The pair couldn’t be separated as they headed into the third session locked at 5-5, but Springer put together a burst of legs, a fifth in a row putting him on the brink of victory at 9-5.

    Cross wasn’t done, putting together three straight legs to close to just a leg behind after dodging a match dart in leg 17, but his race was run a leg later, with Springer finding a 111 finish that confirmed a first PDC Premier Event quarter final.

    2026 Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts
    Wednesday November 18
    4x Round Two Matches
    Niko Springer 10-8 Rob Cross
    Gerwyn Price 10-7 Ryan Searle
    Jermaine Wattimena 10-8 Luke Littler
    Kevin Doets 10-5 Cameron Menzies

    Thursday November 19 (1900 GMT)
    4x Round Two Matches
    Gabriel Clemens v Nathan Aspinall
    Gian van Veen v Martin Schindler
    Luke Humphries v Tom Sykes
    James Wade v Michael van Gerwen
    Best of 19 legs
